title: Printed Melrose arrangements and the Victor reissue
summary: They played printed orchestrations on the Morton dates and added parts; Allen tells him about the Victor reissue of the sides.

bands.name: Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Well, one more question about those jelly roll dates that you've been harping on. Did you ever play any of the arrangements? Some of those were printed that Melrose published.
Did they bring some of those?
Yes, yes, yes. We played quite a few of them. From the orchestration? Or the orchestration, that's right. The printed one? Printed copies, yes.
I thought maybe they came out after the record or I didn't know if the record came out first.

No, he'd... There's several... I remember several tunes there they had. It was printed copies. Printed copies, and you'd play... Play it from there. Yeah, and make up other little parts. Yeah, that's it. Add to it. That's it. Yeah.

Yeah, that's it. Those are certainly wonderful dates. You know, those are out again on Victor now. You can still buy those numbers there. Oh, you? They reissued those. Oh, six months ago some of them came out and you can still... Oh, I see. Some of them like the Black Bottom Stomp, Dr. Jazz, Steamboat. Yeah.
Yeah. I think I'll get them. I'll get them.
It's called Jelly Roll Martin, King of New Orleans Jazz on Victor.
Oh. I... The chant. The chant, yes. Yes. And the pearls. Uh-huh. I'll get those rings because I don't have any of them.
You're just about on all of those except a few of them were made in New York that you weren't on. Two-thirds of them you play the trumpet on. Uh-huh. With Ory and St. Cyr and Simeon and all.
